summary: Verified the legacy-appointments visibility fix end-to-end. Backend: GET /api/appointments returns all 22 appointments (20 expired + 2 pending), every record has a non-null 'status' field (0 missing). Startup logic on server.py L811-820 sets 'pending' for status-less legacy docs and auto-expire logic (L823-840) flips past-dated pending to 'expired'. Frontend Admin Dashboard (superadmin paul.kasawuli) shows: Total Appointments=22, Pending stat=2, 20 gray 'Expired' badges with 'No actions available' text, 2 amber 'Pending' badges. Status filters work: Expired=>20 rows, Pending=>2 rows (with Reject action buttons visible), All=>22 rows. The previously flagged bug in iteration_6 (Pending stat card miscount) now reads 2 correctly.

issues: React hydration warning in console: '<span> cannot be a child of <tbody>' / '<tr> cannot be a child of <span>'. A wrapper <span style={display:contents}> is being rendered between <tbody> and <motion.tr> (likely from a map/Fragment pattern around L723 in AdminDashboard.js). Not blocking rendering but should wrap rows in <AnimatePresence>/<React.Fragment> or move the span to a non-table context.

action_items: Minor (non-blocking): remove the <span data-ve-dynamic> wrapper that is being rendered as a direct child of <tbody> around AdminDashboard.js L723 to clear the React hydration warnings in console.
critical_code_review_comments: Startup migration logic at server.py L811-820 is idempotent and safe to re-run — good.

Auto-expire still only runs at process startup (as flagged in iteration_6). Legacy data is now backfilled, but a long-running process will accumulate past-dated 'pending' rows until next restart. Consider a background scheduler.
server.py now > 900 lines — still exceeds 700-line guideline; split into routers/services.
DEFAULT_ADMIN_ACCOUNTS passwords are still hardcoded (L797-805); should be sourced from env.
seed_data_creation: None. Used existing seeded data (22 appointments).
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 6 test asks are green. Current DB state: 22 appointments, 20 expired (Feb-Mar 2025/2026), 2 pending (Oct 15 2026). Expired filter data-testid='status-filter-expired', Pending filter data-testid='status-filter-pending', All filter data-testid='status-filter-all'. There is a cosmetic React hydration warning from a <span> wrapper inside <tbody> on AdminDashboard.js around line 723 — safe to leave but worth fixing when touching that file.
rca of the issue: RCA (already fixed by main agent): 20 legacy appointments were inserted without a 'status' field. The admin UI only rendered rows whose status matched a known badge, and some code paths treated missing status as unknown, so legacy rows were effectively invisible. Fix in server.py startup: (1) update_many({status:{$exists:false}},{$set:{status:'pending'}}) backfills legacy docs; (2) subsequent auto-expire marks past-dated pending as 'expired'. Verified: API returns 22 docs all with status; UI renders all 22 with correct Expired/Pending badges and the Expired filter button isolates the 20 past-dated rows.
